English language proficiency
International entry requirements
Show menu
International students from non-English speaking backgrounds must meet Adelaide University’s minimum English language requirements to be admitted to a degree.
English language entry requirements are specific to the degree you choose, and some degrees have higher English language requirements. This means the exact level of English language proficiency required will depend upon the degree you are applying to. Adelaide University degree pages list the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) score required and a link to all accepted tests.
You can demonstrate your level of English language proficiency by providing the results of an accepted English language test, noting that only tests taken at an official test centre can be accepted.
Tests are generally valid for two years prior to admission. Some degrees require a shorter validity period. Please visit your chosen degree page for more information.
Accepted tests:
International English Language Testing System (IELTS) - Academic
Pearson Test of English (PTE) Academic
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) – iBT
Cambridge C1 Advanced test (previously Cambridge English: Advanced CAE)
Cambridge C2 Proficiency test
Occupational English Test (OET) (not for all degrees)
Other accepted methods to meet English proficiency:
Australian year 12 with a passing grade in a recognised English as a Second Language or English Language subject
International Baccalaureate Diploma (including specific language subjects undertaken in English)
Foundation program at another Australian university
In limited circumstances, previous academic qualifications or practical application of your English skills in a professional environment

Adelaide University’s English Language Centre (ELC) provides packaged ELICOS programs for students who do not meet English language requirements. Visit the Pathway providers page to find out more.
Adelaide University does not offer packaged programs with The Centre for English Language at the University of South Australia (CELUSA), but does accept CELUSA results.

Primary language pathway*
Alternatively, you may be eligible for a primary language pathway if:
a) English is your primary language; and
b) You have attended and satisfactorily completed at least six years of primary and secondary# education taught and assessed solely in English in a recognised country**.
Notes
*Primary language means the language primarily used for reading, writing, listening, and speaking and the language known best and most comfortable with.
#Secondary Education means Australian school years 7 through 12, even where year 7 is classified as part of primary school in a particular state or territory.
#Six years primary and secondary education means six years of Australian school years 1 through to 12 or the equivalent in a recognised country with two of the years between 7 and 12. Studies to be immediately prior to the intake at discretion of the University.
**Recognised countries: Antigua and Barbuda, Anguilla, Australia, The Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, British Indian Ocean Territory, Canada, Cayman Islands, Dominica, Falkland Islands, Gibraltar, Grenada, Guernsey, Guyana, Isle of Man, Jamaica, Jersey, Malta, New Zealand, Republic of Ireland, Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha, St Kitts and Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines, Trinidad and Tobago, United Kingdom, USA, and US Virgin Islands.
Some other programs have non-standard English language proficiency requirements, please refer to the relevant program degree page for further information.
Current Australian Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) Registration
Evidence of current registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA), showing registration with the NMBA to practice as an Enrolled Nurse (EN), Registered Nurse (RN) or Midwife, without any conditions, relative the specified entry requirements for the program they are applying for.
Research degrees
All research degree students must be proficient in English and meet the minimum English language requirements for their degree. Any applicant who is a citizen and holds a passport from one of the following countries: Australia, Canada (excluding Quebec), New Zealand, the Republic of Ireland, South Africa, the United Kingdom and the United States of America is not required to demonstrate English language proficiency.
Recent academic and/or professional experience
Prior to date of application, the University will not require English Proficiency Test for any applicant who has satisfactorily completed study at a Bachelor degree level or above from one of the following countries: Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Botswana, Canada (excluding Quebec), Cook Islands, Fiji, Gambia, Ghana, Gibraltar, Guyana, Hong Kong, Jamaica, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Malaysia, Mauritius, New Zealand, Nigeria, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Republic of Ireland, Samoa, Seychelles, Singapore, Solomon Islands, South Africa, Tanzania, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, the United Kingdom, the United States of America, Zambia, Zimbabwe for at least one of the last two years, or at least two within the last four years of full-time study.
Applicants who do not meet the above criteria will be required to demonstrate English language proficiency in the form of a valid English test that has been taken within two years preceding the application.
All programs except language rich disciplines require an overall IELTS band score of 6.5 overall, and a minimum of 6.0 in listening, reading, writing and speaking.
Language rich disciplines such as Education, Language and Literature, Communication and Media Studies, and Philosophy and Religious Studies require an overall IELTS band score of 7.0 and a minimum of 6.5 in listening, reading, writing and speaking.
Significant academic teaching experience in English, evaluated and approved case-by-case.
Other significant professional experiences that demonstrate use of English and/or living in an English-speaking country and using English for an extended period of time – to be evaluated and approved case-by-case.
The University only accepts the TOEFL iBT for Australia (0 – 120 score format) conducted at a registered test centre.
As the University is reviewing the structural and scoring changes introduced to the TOEFL iBT test, the 1-6 test format score is not currently accepted. Further updates will be provided in due course.
